Let’s talk ↗

Research Engineer · Fraunhofer IVI

Taehyoung Kim.

I’m a research engineer at Fraunhofer IVI working toward aerial autonomy. My work spans the path from data to deployment: collecting and curating aerial datasets, making multimodal annotation and training more efficient, and developing online perception and mapping alongside offline map reconstruction. I also work on getting these ideas running on real robots, bringing the models and software together into a working system.

The goal is to enable aerial robots to perceive and act, supporting path planning, navigation, and mission execution. I’m also exploring reinforcement learning (RL), vision-language navigation (VLN), and vision-language-action (VLA) models toward end-to-end autonomy, connecting observations and instructions to learned actions.

Here I share the research, experiments, and technical lessons that come out of that process.

01 / A little about me

From an idea
to a working system.

My research brings together video understanding, multimodal sensing, and semantic 3D mapping. I’m interested in connecting these ideas to perception systems that work beyond a benchmark.

This site is a place to share that process: the papers, the experiments, and the practical things I learn while building. It also leaves room for side projects and ideas outside my day-to-day research.
